WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
The LORD calls him "Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant", and says "have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar". Jeremiah 25:9 Jeremiah 27:6
Daniel to the king: "Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory"; "Thou art this head of gold." Daniel 2:37–38
Ezra 5:12: God "gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house, and carried the people away into Babylon". Ezra 5:12
Daniel 5 recalls that "when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne", till he knew that the most high God ruled. Daniel 5:20–21
His own last words in Daniel: "Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven … and those that walk in pride he is able to abase." Daniel 4:37
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
He put the temple vessels in "the house of his god"; Cyrus later brought them out. Daniel 1:2 2 Chronicles 36:7 Ezra 1:7
His decree: anyone who spoke amiss against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego would be cut in pieces, "because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort". Daniel 3:29
He sent a letter "unto all people, nations, and languages" telling "the signs and wonders that the high God hath wrought toward me". Daniel 4:1–3
"Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power". Daniel 4:30
Jehoiakim served him three years, then rebelled. 2 Kings 24:1
Jeremiah told Zedekiah: "Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live." Jeremiah 27:12
Zedekiah rebelled against him, "who had made him swear by God". 2 Chronicles 36:13 2 Kings 24:20
He carried away Jerusalem's princes, mighty men, craftsmen and smiths; "none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land". 2 Kings 24:14
From the textJeremiah 52 counts 4,600 persons carried away in his 7th, 18th and 23rd years; Kings gives 10,000 for the first deportation alone. Jeremiah 52:28–30 2 Kings 24:14
He made Daniel ruler over the province of Babylon and set Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego over its affairs. Daniel 2:48–49
Ezra and Nehemiah list "the children of the province" whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away, who came back. Ezra 2:1 Nehemiah 7:6

DOUGHERTY (1929)
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given

His first year = Jehoiakim's fourth (Jer 25:1); Jehoiachin taken in his eighth (2 Kgs 24:12); Zedekiah's tenth = his eighteenth (Jer 32:1); the temple burned in his nineteenth (2 Kgs 25:8); deportations in his 7th, 18th and 23rd (Jer 52:28–30).
DRIVER (1900)
BABYLONIAN CHRONICLE 5
No years given[40][1]
Crown prince at Carchemish in 605 BC; on his father's death he returned and took the throne the same year (Wiseman's edition, facts only).
The two verses
Daniel 1:1; Jeremiah 25:1 and 46:2

Daniel: "In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim … came Nebuchadnezzar". Jeremiah: Jehoiakim's fourth year "was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar", the year of Carchemish. Daniel 1:1 Jeremiah 25:1 Jeremiah 46:2
"Came" means set out
E. W. Hengstenberg, C. F. Keil and O. Zöckler (as reported by S. R. Driver, 1900); Ellicott's commentary
The word "came" marks the starting point: Nebuchadnezzar set out from Babylon in Jehoiakim's third year and reached Judah after Carchemish in the fourth. Daniel 1:1 [92][9]
The end of the third, the start of the fourth
John Gill (1748–63)
Gill places the event at the close of Jehoiakim's third year and the beginning of the fourth, "which was the first of Nebuchadnezzar". Daniel 1:1 Jeremiah 25:1 [56]
Daniel's date is doubtful
S. R. Driver (1900)

Driver held the date historically doubtful: it rests on a tradition also found in 2 Chronicles 36:6–7, and the invasion of 2 Kings 24:1 belongs after Jehoiakim's fourth year. Daniel 1:1 2 Chronicles 36:6–7 [92]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how long Nebuchadnezzar reigned or how he died.
Scripture does not name his father.
Daniel does not say how long "seven times" is.
Scripture does not say whether his campaign against Egypt took place as Jeremiah and Ezekiel foretold it.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textEzekiel always, and Jeremiah mostly, spell his name Nebuchadrezzar; Kings, Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah, Esther and Daniel spell it Nebuchadnezzar, as Jeremiah does in chapters 27–29 and at 34:1 and 39:5.
